properties.name: MEASURED 2026-09-22: tools/test_nudge_path.py's no-hook handshake test failed on the dev box and passes in CI, because the server counts a machine-wide OpenCode plugin installed there at 11:28 the same day
properties.statement: test_a_project_with_no_hook_is_told_so_at_handshake builds a bare temp project and expects the "REFLOW2 HAS NOT INSTALLED" advisory. On this box it got none. nudge::status_with_home returns Installed when ~/.config/opencode/plugins/reflow2-loop-nudge.js exists, and that file was written 2026-09-22 11:28 — so the test read the developer's machine, not the project it built. Refuted alternatives: unsetting CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and TMPDIR changed nothing; giving the server HOME=<the temp project> made 9/9 pass. Fixed in the test (HOME isolated), not in the server: counting a machine-wide plugin is the documented, correct behaviour (PR #511). Unrelated to the loop-closure work; found while gating it.
